results.title: Using Social Media for Smoking Cessation: Evidence from Digital ...
results.content: This chapter reviews the expanding evidence on social media-based smoking cessation interventions, with particular attention to their theoretical foundations, implementation approaches, effectiveness across different platforms, and economic implications. By summarizing current knowledge and outlining future research directions, this chapter aims to inform and support the development of effective social media-based interventions to assist individuals and communities in quitting smoking, particularly in settings where traditional cessation resources may be limited. Robust methodology is essential to evaluating social media-based smoking cessation interventions, requiring careful attention to study design, outcome measurement, and engagement assessment. The effectiveness of social media-based smoking cessation interventions varies across platforms, study designs, and populations. Additional priorities include developing standardized engagement metrics to facilitate cross-study comparisons, exploring implementation strategies for integrating social media interventions into healthcare systems, and designing interventions that address health equity concerns to ensure digital approaches reduce rather than exacerbate existing disparities in cessation support. ### 5.1 Social media-based interventions: The WeChat smoking cessation study.

results.content: This major proposed rule addresses: changes to the physician fee schedule (PFS); other changes to Medicare Part B payment policies to ensure that payment systems are updated to reflect changes in medical practice, relative value of services, and changes in the statute; codification of establishment of new policies for: the Medicare Prescription Drug Inflation Rebate Program under the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022; the Ambulatory Specialty Model; updates to the Medicare Diabetes Prevention Program expanded model; updates to drugs and biological products paid under Part B; Medicare Shared Savings Program requirements; updates to the Quality Payment Program; updates to policies for Rural Health Clinics and Federally Qualified Health Centers update to the Ambulance Fee Schedule regulations; codification of the Inflation Reduction Act and Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2023 provisions; updates to the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program. See also, Data.CMS.gov, Medicare Shared Savings Program, Accountable Care Organizations, Public Use File (by performance year), available at *https://data.cms.gov/​medicare-shared-savings-program/​accountable-care-organizations.* We note that some observations described in this section of this proposed rule, particularly for PY 2025 data, are based on internal analysis.
